'''Octavio Augusto Novaro Peñalosa'''  (4 July 1939 – 6 March 2018) was a prominent theoretical [[physicist]] specialized in theoretical  [[catalysis]],  [[physical chemistry]],  [[biophysics]]  and  [[geophysics]]. He received the [[National Prize for Arts and Sciences]] in 1983 and became the first [[Mexico|Mexican]] researcher to receive the [[UNESCO Science Prize]] in 1993. Since 1995 he was also one of the forty lifetime members of [[Colegio Nacional (Mexico)|The National College]].<ref name="curriculum"/>

Novaro Peñalosa was born in [[Mexico City]] and graduated from the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] with a bachelor's degree (1965), a master's degree (1968) and a doctorate degree in Physics (1969) under the supervision of [[Marcos Moshinsky]]. Later on, he worked in [[postdoctoral research]] programs in [[Sweden]], [[Italy]], [[Turkey]] and the [[United States]].<ref name="curriculum"/>

He worked as a professor researcher at the National Autonomous University of Mexico since 1971 and for over fifteen years he worked and advised the [[Mexican Institute of Petroleum]], where he designed several catalysts used in the [[petrochemical industry]].<ref>{{cite web|author = Institute of Physics (UNAM) | title = Biography | url = http://www.fisica.unam.mx/departamentos/teorica/index.php?option=com_investigadores&idInvestigador=83&Itemid=30 | language = Spanish | accessdate=2008-06-13 }}</ref> During his career he published over 225 articles, 4 books, obtained 4 [[patent]]s and some of his former students have become [[Rector (academia)|rector]]s in [[China]] or heads of laboratories in [[France]], [[Poland]] and [[Scotland]].<ref name="curriculum"/>

According to his résumé, he was also an accomplished [[Multilingualism|polyglot]] fluent in [[Spanish (language)|Spanish]], [[English (language)|English]], [[French (language)|French]], [[Italian (language)|Italian]] and [[Portuguese (language)|Portuguese]]; translated, read and wrote [[German (language)|German]], [[Russian (language)|Russian]] and [[Greek (language)|Greek]] and spoke both [[Chinese (language)|Chinese]] and [[Japanese (language)|Japanese]].<ref name="curriculum"/>
